definitions.meaning: grammar calls the word 'the' the ... article, so this describes the kind of article it is
firm here means fixed or settled, as in a firm date

explanation.surface: A query about what kind of article a famous company title like 'The Firm' is.
explanation.walkthrough: The quote marks hide the split: 'The' is the grammatical article, and 'Firm' stands alone as the second definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: grammar's name for the article 'the', and an adjective meaning fixed or decided.

parts.note: a dam blocks a river
to ask is to request

explanation.surface: Someone stopping a request for some cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: A rich patterned fabric of silk or linen, named after Damascus, is a material.

clue.text: Split in favour of King Edward's divorcee initially

parts.note: for means supporting, in favour of
K is the chess abbreviation for king

indicators.note: initially means take the opening letters of the following words

explanation.surface: Evokes the abdication crisis, when Edward VIII gave up the throne for the divorcee Wallis Simpson.
explanation.definitionFit: A forked road or tongue is divided into two branches, that is, split.

parts.note: well known, but for bad reasons rather than good ones

explanation.surface: A paradoxical phrase for a celebrity with a bad name.
explanation.definitionFit: This adjective describes someone widely known for something shameful, fame earned through infamy.

clue.text: The first Russian ready to meet Creator — he disturbs the peace

indicators.note: 'The first' asks for only the opening letter of the word The

parts.note: ready is slang for cash, and the rouble is Russia's currency
the Maker is God the Creator

explanation.surface: A Russian prepared to meet his Maker, i.e. die, is a figure causing a stir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ready' is British slang for money ('the readies'), so 'Russian ready' is the rouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who stirs up strife and disrupts order is a disturber of the peace.

definitions.meaning: lofty means high up, in the air
an antenna is the rod that picks up radio or TV signals

explanation.surface: A description of a tall radio mast.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: an adjective for something high up in the air, and the British noun for a radio or TV receiving rod.

indicators.note: therein says the answer lies inside the words just given

explanation.surface: Instructions to place a puzzle inside something so it can be solved.
explanation.definitionFit: To embed something is to fix it firmly in position within something else.

clue.text: Imaginative ticket tout almost got in, dressed like Wayne Rooney

indicators.note: got in says one piece has been placed inside the other

parts.note: Wayne Rooney played for Manchester United, who wear red, so in red

indicators.note: almost means the word falls one letter short of complete

parts.note: a spiv is a flashy small-time dealer, like a ticket tout

explanation.surface: A tout sneaks into a match wearing a footballer's kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the tout's last letter; 'got in' places the rest within the outfit. A spiv is a British word for a flashy black-market dealer. Wayne Rooney was an England footballer famous at Manchester United, whose shirts are red.
explanation.definitionFit: Inspired work is creative and brilliantly original, which is to say imaginative.

clue.text: Huge ship laden with oriental generosity

indicators.note: a ship laden with cargo carries it, here the oriental letter follows the ship

parts.note: huge means large
SS, steamship, is the standard abbreviation for a ship
E for eastern, i.e. oriental

explanation.surface: A great vessel loaded with eastern goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Largesse is liberal giving of money or gifts, a show of generosity.

clue.text: Running event may damage a short sexy beachwear

parts.note: to mar is to damage or spoil

indicators.note: short means the word loses its final letter, cut off at the end

parts.note: a thong is a skimpy swimsuit bottom

explanation.surface: A warning that skimpy swimwear could ruin a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' removes the G from THONG, giving THON.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-distance road race of about 26 miles is the classic running event of this name.

clue.text: He berates sailor, a drug addict

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is the standard abbreviation for a sailor
a user is slang for someone who takes drugs

explanation.surface: A man scolding a sailor who is hooked on drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who berates others hurls insults at them, which is verbal mistreatment.

indicators.note: unruly means disorderly, so the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: A Scottish minister in tartan who refuses to toe the line.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone stubbornly uncooperative and resistant to authority is defiant.

definitions.meaning: to spread is to daub or apply thinly, as butter on bread
a malicious untrue story put about to damage someone

explanation.surface: An instruction to put a lie about.
explanation.definitionFit: A verb for daubing something over a surface, and a noun for a slanderous claim meant to discredit someone.

clue.text: You really need to be on this

definitions.text: You really need to be on this

parts.words: You really need to be on this
parts.note: being on the subsistence threshold means being so poor you truly are in need

explanation.surface: Seems to be urging someone that a course or plan is essential for them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Really need' reads as strong advice; actually it means being genuinely needy, i.e. living at the poverty level.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase 'on the' this describes people at the minimum level of income needed to live, so they really are in need.

indicators.note: frenzied means wildly agitated, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A frantic conductor is told to calm down.
explanation.definitionFit: Temperance is restraint and avoiding excess, the quality of being moderate.

clue.text: Exclusion of retina from clinical experimentation; yes, exclusion

indicators.note: exclusion of names the letters to be removed from the fodder
from points to the long word the removed letters come out of, the rest then rearranged

explanation.surface: A medical trial that leaves out tests on the eye's retina.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the letters of RETINA from EXPERIMENTATION, not as one run, and rearrange what is left (EXPEMTION); 'clinical' and 'yes' only dress the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: An exemption is a release from a duty or rule, being excluded from it.

clue.text: A mammal flying blindly to Irish slaughterhouse

parts.note: a bat is the flying mammal, proverbially blind

explanation.surface: A creature blundering into an Irish abattoir.
explanation.definitionFit: An abattoir is a place where animals are killed for meat, a slaughterhouse.

clue.text: When accepting support, naval lieutenant raised friction

parts.note: as means when, as in 'as I left'
a bra is a supporting undergarment

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the letters are read upwards, i.e. backwards

parts.note: the first lieutenant in a ship is called Number One, abbreviated No I

explanation.surface: A naval officer's promotion causing friction.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Royal Navy the first lieutenant is 'Number One', written NO I; 'raised' turns this up the column.
explanation.definitionFit: Abrasion is the wearing away of a surface by rubbing, which is friction.

clue.text: Recant shabby arrangement for one with a young bride

indicators.note: an arrangement of letters is a new ordering of them

explanation.surface: Someone being told to withdraw a shabby agreement on behalf of another.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal, mocking term for a person whose partner is much younger than they are.

parts.note: bananas is slang for crazy

parts.note: the end is the outcome or result

explanation.surface: A guard who is sick of how things turned out.

indicators.note: 'at work' signals the letters being worked over into a new order; 'at' is part of the fodder

explanation.walkthrough: 'at' belongs to the fodder, so the indicator is just 'work'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something passing and short-lived, lasting only briefly, is temporary.

clue.text: Quiet! I need half the light

indicators.note: half the word means its first two of four letters

explanation.definitionFit: Shine is brightness or radiance, a sense of light.

explanation.surface: Someone managed to grab a little sleep.

explanation.definitionFit: A warden who patrols and looks after a national park or forest has this job title.

definitions.meaning: classic as in a recognised model or benchmark
a regiment's colours are its flag

explanation.surface: Seems to describe a timeless colour scheme.
